title: Verifiable Supply Chain and Distribution
objective: Automate canonical cross-platform builds, provenance, SBOM, signatures/attestations, and channel-aware installers.

stories.title: Release artifact manifest
stories.outcome: Define canonical artifact names, checksums, target triples, channel, source SHA, build identity, and knowledge compatibility metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Every distributed binary is represented exactly once.
verification: Manifest schema and checksum round-trip tests.

stories.title: Automated multi-target build
stories.outcome: Use a release toolchain such as dist/cargo-dist or equivalent to produce macOS/Linux/Windows artifacts and installers from tags.
acceptance_criteria: Build matrix covers declared tier-1 targets.
Release process is reproducible from a clean tagged checkout.
verification: Release dry-run workflow and installer smoke tests.

stories.title: Provenance, SBOM, and signing
stories.outcome: Generate GitHub artifact attestations/provenance, SBOM, and cryptographic verification material for canonical artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Users can verify origin from repository/workflow/commit.
SBOM is attached/attested for each canonical build family.
Release fails if required evidence is missing.

stories.title: Installation-source awareness
stories.outcome: Record Homebrew/direct/Windows/Linux package source and route upgrade guidance through the same source.
acceptance_criteria: cancellai update --check never silently switches package channels.
Source is inspectable in version/status output.

stories.title: Stable/beta/nightly authority constraints
stories.outcome: Bind release channel to maximum default authority.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly defaults cannot execute stable-equivalent irreversible autonomy.
Channel information is signed/attested release metadata.

stories.title: Canonical source and distribution repository topology
stories.outcome: Move the canonical cross-platform product source to a product-named repository when Rust becomes canonical while preserving homebrew-cancellai as a compatibility/distribution tap rather than forcing a premature repository migration.
acceptance_criteria: The migration plan preserves tags/releases/issues or documents intentional moves and does not break existing Homebrew users.
The canonical source repository is unambiguously identified by release provenance and contributor documentation.
homebrew-cancellai remains usable as a tap or is retired only through an explicit compatibility plan.
verification: Repository/tap release dry-run and existing Homebrew upgrade-path smoke test.

stories.title: Safety incident containment and capability downgrade
stories.outcome: Operationalize a least-authority incident path that can stop promotion and remotely distribute signed capability downgrades without introducing a remote destructive control plane.
acceptance_criteria: A compromised provider/version/capability can be downgraded to Observe or Recommend through trusted signed knowledge without granting any new mutation authority.
Offline operation remains available under the installed local safety kernel when the knowledge service is unavailable.
Incident evidence records affected release/knowledge provenance, capability, provider, platform, and invariant references without collecting provider payload content.
verification: Replay, rollback, invalid-signature, unavailable-network, and attempted authority-elevation incident simulations.
